name: 80K Hours Upskilling Resources
current_details: A curated 80,000 Hours list of 67 resources for upskilling in technical AI safety, spanning field overviews, courses (ARENA, BlueDot, Karpathy's Zero to Hero), project ideas in evals and mech interp, researcher advice, fellowships (Anthropic, MATS, Astra, LASR, SPAR, Pivotal, ERA, CHAI), and org profiles. Free, self-paced, with links to 1-on-1 career advising.

name: 80K Hours AI Safety Career Review
current_details: A 80,000 Hours career review on technical AI safety research, covering empirical (open to strong software engineers, even without ML backgrounds) and theoretical paths (for strong maths/theoretical CS backgrounds or top-10 ML PhD candidates). Covers impact, downsides, earnings, personal fit, PhD decisions, job hunting and key organisations. Notes only ~300 people worked on the field as of 2022.

name: AISafety.com Events & Training
current_deadline: Updated continuously — next listed deadline 20 Nov 2026
current_details: AISafety.com's continuously updated directory lists 120 AI safety training programs — fellowships, bootcamps, courses and workshops, online and in person — of which 58 are upcoming, filterable by type, focus, entry bar, stipend, length and location. The site also tracks 37 events, 575 jobs, 61 funding sources, 270 communities and a 380-entry field map.

structured.program_dates: Rolling cohorts; current listings start Nov 2026 – Oct 2027

name: AISafety.com Self-Study
current_details: A curated directory of 29 self-study curricula and reading lists for learning AI safety independently. Spans general introductions (BlueDot's Future of AI, Lens Academy's AI Risk Fundamentals, DeepMind's 75-minute AGI Safety Short Course, AI Safety Atlas, CAIS's AISES), technical alignment (ARENA, Intro to ML Safety, Harvard CS 2881, Stanford, XLab) and governance/strategy material. Each entry is tagged by category and type; no application or deadline.

name: Apart Research Hackathons
current_deadline: Next Sprint: Threat Intelligence & Threat Modelling Hackathon, Dec 4–6, 2026
current_details: Apart Research runs weekend research sprints (hackathons) tackling a single AI safety question, open to anyone worldwide, online and at local in-person sites. Standouts are invited to Apart Studio, the route into the Apart Fellowship; Partnered Fellowships take direct applications. Research focuses on manipulation and dark patterns in frontier AI systems.

name: BlueDot Impact
current_deadline: Nov 22, 2026 (Technical AI Safety & Biosecurity); AGI Strategy Nov 29; Frontier AI Governance Dec 6, 2026 — grants rolling
current_details: BlueDot Impact runs free cohort-based online courses in AGI Strategy, Technical AI Safety, Frontier AI Governance and Biosecurity — 25–40 hours each, done in one intensive week or part-time with facilitated small groups. It also offers in-person programs (Incubator Week in San Francisco, AI Security Bootcamp) and rolling grants of $20k–$200k (Rapid Grants up to $20k).

structured.stipend: Grants $20k–$200k; Rapid Grants up to $20k; up to $200k for Incubator Week pitches
structured.location: Online; in-person in San Francisco (Incubator Week)
structured.program_dates: Rolling cohorts; Incubator Week and AI Security Bootcamp dates listed on site

name: Google DeepMind: AGI Safety Short Course
current_details: A free, self-paced introductory course on AGI safety from Google DeepMind's safety research team, comprising ~75 minutes of short recorded talks and exercises plus a slide deck and exercise workbook. It covers the path to superhuman capabilities, risks from deliberate planning and instrumental subgoals, how misaligned goals arise (specification gaming vs. goal misgeneralization), DeepMind's technical alignment approach (amplified oversight, robust training & monitoring, security & control, interpretability, safer design patterns, alignment stress tests), and its governance approach including frontier safety practices and dangerous capability evaluations. Aimed at students, researchers and professionals who want an accessible one-hour introduction to AI alignment.

name: MATS Slack #opportunities
current_details: Contract work, facilitation gigs, paper reviews, and collaboration opportunities from the MATS community.

name: Outsider's Roadmap to AI Safety (LessWrong)
current_details: A comprehensive guide published in July 2025 for professionals transitioning into AI safety research from technical backgrounds such as software engineering, physics, or data science. Covers three critical domains: interpretability research (reverse-engineering AI systems to understand their inner workings), alignment research (ensuring AI systems remain beneficial and share human values), and AI control & governance (technical policy for advanced systems). Written by someone actively making the transition, synthesizing insights from Neel Nanda's mechanistic interpretability resources, 80,000 Hours career research, and the broader alignment community, with practical advice on evolving roles (the shift from separate research engineers/scientists toward 'full-stack researchers'), required skills, and pathways for newcomers to contribute meaningfully to the field.

name: Anthropic Fellows Program
current_details: Anthropic Fellows funds and mentors engineers and researchers working on priority AI safety questions — scalable oversight, AI control, model organisms, interpretability, AI security, and model welfare. Fellows spend 4 months on empirical research with an Anthropic mentor, receiving ~$15K/month compute funding plus a stipend. No PhD or prior ML experience required.

name: CBAI AI Safety Research Fellowship
current_deadline: Applications closed — next cohort summer 2027; EOI form open
current_details: Cambridge Boston Alignment Initiative's ten-week, fully-funded in-person research fellowship in Cambridge, MA, spanning technical AI safety, governance and technical governance. Fellows get $12,500 stipend, housing for relocators, meals, Harvard Square office, weekly mentorship, and ~$1,500/week compute, plus possible extension funding up to 6 months.

structured.program_dates: Oct 13 – Dec 18, 2026 (Fall 2026 cohort); next cohort summer 2027

name: ERA Fellowship (Cambridge)
current_deadline: Closed — Winter 2027 cycle runs Jan 18 – Mar 26, 2027
current_details: The ERA:AI Fellowship is a 10-week full-time research programme in Cambridge, UK across three tracks: technical AI safety, AI governance, and technical AI governance. Fellows receive a competitive stipend, meals, covered transport and visas, research management support, a compute budget, expert mentorship, and 30+ community events alongside 200+ alumni.

name: Iliad Intensive / Fellowship
current_details: Iliad runs in-house AI alignment research and training programs. The Iliad Fellowship helps technically strong scholars pivot into mathematical and theoretical alignment over ~12 weeks in London or the Bay Area; Fellows must first complete the month-long Iliad Intensive. Research spans learning theory, debate, heuristic arguments, data attribution, agency, and neural network geometry. About half of Fellows receive a six-month extension.

name: MATS (ML Alignment Theory Scholars)
current_deadline: Closed - check for next cycle (mentor applications open for Summer & Autumn 2027)
current_details: MATS is an independent research fellowship pairing talented researchers with top mentors in machine alignment, transparency, and security. Fellows conduct research for 12 weeks in Berkeley, CA and London, UK, with the chance to apply for an additional 6–12 month funded extension. MATS also runs a Residency for long-horizon AI safety research.

name: AE Studio — AI Alignment Research Grants
current_details: The AI Alignment Foundation (spun out of AE Studio) funds high-risk, high-reward alignment research beyond interpretability, evals, and control, pairing researchers with dedicated engineering teams that can execute ideas with as little as one hour per week of your time. Open to alignment researchers and technical experts from other fields; applications accepted via open form.

name: Pivotal Research Fellowship
current_deadline: Applications closed for the 18 Jan – 30 Apr 2027 cohort — expression of interest open
current_details: A 15-week full-time, in-person AI safety research fellowship in London at LISA, with weekly 1-on-1 mentorship, dedicated research managers, workshops and speaker sessions. Fellows receive a £15,000–£18,000 stipend, travel, £1,800/month housing for non-London fellows, weekday meals and compute. Open to anyone 18+ from any academic background.

name: Second Look Research (UChicago XLab)
current_details: Second Look Research, a project of UChicago's Existential Risk Lab, produces open-source replications of load-bearing empirical AI safety results. Its Second Look Fellows program is a 10-week, in-person research program at the University of Chicago where each fellow owns replication projects from scoping through implementation and write-up.

name: SPAR
current_deadline: Spring 2027 applications open December 16, 2026 and close January 13, 2027 (mentor/org applications close November 30, 2026)
current_details: SPAR, run by Kairos, is a 3-month remote fellowship pairing students and professionals with experienced mentors on AI safety, policy, biosecurity, communications and fieldbuilding projects. Fellows commit 5–40 hours/week alongside other work and present at a virtual Demo Day with $7,000 in prizes. Open to all experience levels; an expression-of-interest form is live for Spring 2027.

name: Foresight Institute AI Nodes
current_details: Foresight Institute's AI for Science & Safety Nodes RFP offers grant funding, office space, and private local compute at hubs in San Francisco and Berlin, plus a community xNode in Cape Town. Calls cover local compute, coordination and accountability, and AI-first science (bio, neuro, nano). Grants typically $30K–$100K; review takes about three months. Ongoing expressions of interest accepted for launching independent AI Nodes.

name: Manifund Regranting
current_details: Manifund pairs AI safety experts with independent regranting budgets of $100K–$350K, sourced from their own networks or Manifund's open call. Single-owner budgets mean grants land in days, not months, with example regrants from $11K to $200K. Its 501c3 fiscal sponsorship covers individuals, unregistered projects and (pending diligence) for-profits; all grants and rationales are published publicly.

name: Meridian Cambridge — Research Accelerator Week
current_details: An intensive 6-day programme in Cambridge, UK that moves technical AI safety researchers into funded independent research via a dedicated Coefficient Giving funding pathway. Participants meet 30+ researchers, form teams, submit an EOI on Day 3, and leave with a completed grant proposal, plus Meridian fiscal sponsorship and automatic consideration for a 3-12 month Visiting Researcher residency. Accommodation, meals, visa and travel costs covered.

structured.stipend: Travel reimbursed up to £200 UK / £400 Europe / £700 international; accommodation and meals covered

name: Schmidt Sciences — Trustworthy AI RFP
current_details: Schmidt Sciences posts its current open funding calls here, noting it proactively seeks out grant opportunities and does not accept unsolicited proposals. No open calls are currently listed — including no Trustworthy AI / AI & Advanced Computing RFP. Researchers can subscribe to the AI & Advanced Computing newsletter for alerts on new calls.

name: Schmidt Sciences — Scaling AI Safety for a Multi-Agent World
current_deadline: Closed — deadline was August 9, 2026 11:59 PM AoE
current_details: A joint funding call supporting foundational research on safety in multi-principal, multi-agent AI ecosystems. Two tiers: Tier 1 up to $300,000 and Tier 2 $300,000–$1,000,000, for 1–2 year projects across four clusters — sandboxes and testbeds, the science of agent networks, agent infrastructure, and multi-agent oversight and control. Decisions expected Autumn 2026.

name: Survival & Flourishing Fund (SFF)
current_deadline: Closed — 2026 Main Round applications closed April 22, 2026; next round not yet announced
current_details: SFF organizes S-Process grant rounds funding organizations working on the long-term survival and flourishing of sentient life, having directed ~$216MM to date. The 2026 Main Round is complete, distributing $63.64MM — far above its $14–28MM estimate. A rolling application remains for Speculation Grants and Matching Pledges, and SFC is offering a $5–20MM ISPA Inspection Prize.

structured.program_dates: 2026 round recommendations announced; next round expected 2027

name: Catalyze Impact
current_details: Catalyze Impact is a 501(c)(3) non-profit incubator that helps exceptional founders launch AI safety and resilience organizations, helping them pick the right problem and connecting them to funders and domain experts. Since 2023 it has helped launch 20+ organizations that raised over $190M. Its two Funding Networks (investors and grantmakers, $50K+/yr) run 2–4 rounds a year.

structured.stipend: $50K–$300K typical launch funding via Funding Network

name: Halcyon Futures
current_details: Halcyon Futures is a grant-maker, incubator and investment firm backing exceptional founders building in AI safety, cybersecurity and biosecurity. It combines grants, incubation support and venture investment to build resilience for the era of transformative AI. Prospective founders can reach the team directly at hello@halcyonfutures.org.

name: ImpactOps
current_details: Impact Ops is an operations consultancy giving hands-on specialist support to high-impact organizations across AI safety, global health, animal welfare and climate. Services cover six areas: finance, recruitment, entity setup and fiscal-sponsor spin-outs, donor/grantee due diligence, ops audits, and systems implementation. Clients include CLTR, BlueDot Impact, Foresight Institute, Longview Philanthropy and The Earthshot Prize. Careers and contact pages available.

name: Rethink Priorities Special Projects
current_details: Rethink Priorities' Special Projects Program offers fiscal sponsorship and end-to-end operations for high-impact initiatives: tax-exempt grant receipt, accounting, US/UK or Employer-of-Record hiring, visa support, fundraising coordination, and event planning. Fees typically around 14% of project costs. Through end of 2025: 195 expressions of interest, 15 projects supported, $19.7M expended, 114 sponsee staff onboarded.

structured.location: US & UK entities; international hiring via Employer of Record

name: Seldon Lab
current_details: Seldon Lab is an accelerator and venture studio backing founders building AI security and existential safety technologies for world-scale AGI deployment. Beyond capital and mentorship, the team publishes research, builds systems, and deploys cyber-physical infrastructure. Portfolio companies include Lucid Computing and Andon Labs; applications are accepted on a rolling basis via the Apply Now page.

name: WorkStream
current_details: WorkStream Nonprofit (High Impact Alliance, 501(c)(3)) provides operations consulting and embedded support for small and mid-sized nonprofits: workflow optimization, fractional COO leadership, technology implementation, executive support, and hiring. Its flagship six-month Operations Accelerator offers workshops, coaching, and peer accountability for teams of 4-20 staff, alongside the 10-indicator GRIP growth-readiness assessment and fiscal sponsorship pathways. Conversations start on a rolling basis.

name: 80,000 Hours Job Board
current_details: A handpicked, continuously updated board of high-impact roles, with heavy emphasis on AI safety, AI policy and existential risk. Filter by annualised USD salary, location and role type, exclude career-development roles, save or hide listings, and get matches based on your background. Includes daily/weekly job alerts, free 1-1 career advice and an AI advisor chat.

name: AISafety.com Jobs
current_details: A continuously updated AI safety job board listing 575 open roles (plus 5 more) across research, policy, engineering, operations, communications and security. Current postings include MIT FutureTech, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, FAR AI, Encode, Mycelium, Constellation, Global Shield and Canada's NRC, with pay from $90,000 to $450,000 (UK roles to £640,000). Many roles are remote and non-technical.

structured.location: Global — SF Bay Area, London, Washington DC, Boston, Ottawa, Canberra, Europe & remote

name: Center for AI Safety (CAIS)
current_details: The Center for AI Safety (CAIS) is a San Francisco-based non-profit reducing societal-scale AI risks through research, field-building, and advocacy. Its careers page lists no specific open roles but invites interested candidates to email hiring@safe.ai; researchers can submit a collaboration form to work with CAIS.

name: FAR AI Careers
current_details: FAR.AI's careers landing page invites applicants to join its mission for trustworthy and secure AI, spanning research agendas, global AI events, and field-building programs. No individual roles, deadlines, salaries, or locations are listed here — specific openings appear elsewhere on the site and are typically filled on a rolling basis.

name: MATS Alumni Hiring Database
current_details: A signup form to create an account for the MATS Alumni Hiring Database, which connects MATS (ML Alignment & Theory Scholars) alumni with organizations hiring in AI safety. Registration requires only a full name, email, and agreement to the MATS Privacy Policy. Exclusively for MATS program alumni.

name: MATS Careers (Staff Hiring)
current_details: MATS is the Berkeley-based AI safety research mentorship program, and its careers page covers staff hiring. The page says MATS is actively hiring across a variety of roles, but lists no specific openings — applicants are directed to a general Expression of Interest form, reviewed as positions open. MATS seeks people motivated by AI alignment, transparency, and security.

name: What AI Safety Orgs Want in a Hire
current_details: 80,000 Hours blog post (September 23, 2025) summarising a survey of 38 AI safety org leaders on hiring needs. Finds 1–3 years of relevant or policy experience often suffices outside technical research, recommends BlueDot, Talos, MATS, GovAI, ERA:AI and Pivotal fellowships, and urges publishing work publicly and networking. Links to 300+ AI safety roles on the job board.

name: Apollo Research
current_details: Apollo Research hires across technical research, engineering, governance, and operations on AI scheming, deception, AI control, and loss-of-control risks, plus its Watcher product. Most staff work from London or San Francisco with regular in-office days; benefits include equity, pension/401(k) matching, unlimited PTO, private medical insurance, and 6 months paid parental leave. Visa sponsorship offered; no internships.

name: Beneficial AI Foundation
current_details: The Beneficial AI Foundation is hiring fully remote roles researching how to keep AI beneficial for generations to come. Open positions: AI Safety Research Scientist (starting at $35–$75/hour, depending on experience) and Research Engineer (starting at $30–$70/hour, based on track record). Both are remote from anywhere with no stated deadline.

name: Forethought
current_details: Forethought Research is a non-profit studying how to navigate rapid AI progress and the transition to superintelligent AI. Three openings have no application deadline: a general researcher expression of interest, one on extreme power concentration, and a Founders Fellowship. Based in Oxford or Berkeley (remote negotiable, UK visa sponsorship usually available), with 33 days leave and a £5k/yr development budget.

name: Goodfire
current_details: Goodfire is an AI interpretability startup hiring agentic, mission-driven people to advance understanding of AI systems, with product lines spanning LLMs and life sciences. All roles are full-time, in person five days a week at their San Francisco (Telegraph Hill) office. The careers page's live listings failed to load; the full role listing is hosted on Greenhouse.

name: Gray Swan AI
current_details: Gray Swan AI is an AI security company building adversarial evaluation and red-teaming tools (Shade, Cygnal, and the Arena red-teaming network), with research informing safety evaluations of frontier models. The careers page highlights Software Engineer openings, reviewed on a rolling basis. Benefits include 28 days off, 401(k) with 4% matching, visa sponsorship, flexible work, and 100% paid parental leave with up to 14 weeks birthing leave.

name: LawZero
current_details: LawZero is a non-profit AI safety lab founded by Yoshua Bengio, based in Montreal with many roles also in Berlin, building safe-by-design, non-agentic AI for scientific discovery and oversight of agentic systems. Its job board lists around 15 openings across research, ML engineering, legal, communications and operations, plus a 2027 internship expression-of-interest form and Talent Community sign-up.

name: METR (formerly ARC Evals)
current_details: METR is a research nonprofit measuring AI capabilities, autonomy and loss-of-control risk, contributing to evaluation standards (STREAM, AEF-1) and frontier safety policies. Open roles: Member of Policy Staff, Government Affairs (Washington, D.C., $306K–$471K), Head of Development ($206K–$306K) and Head of People ($223K–$260K) in Berkeley, plus a General Expression of Interest. Benefits include 401k 100% match up to 8%, 21-week parental leave and unlimited PTO.

name: MIRI TGT Research Fellowship
current_deadline: Closed - register interest for future cohorts
current_details: MIRI's Technical Governance Team fellowship pairs fellows with scoped projects at the intersection of technical and political AI governance — GPU training detection, chip production monitoring, verification mechanisms, and U.S. executive legal powers. Runs 8 weeks at 40 hrs/week with a $1,200/week stipend ($9,600), remote-by-default with a Berkeley kickoff week. No visa sponsorship.

structured.location: Remote with in-person kickoff week in Berkeley, CA
structured.program_dates: An 8-week period between Feb 2 and Aug 31, 2026

name: Redwood Research
current_details: Redwood Research, a nonprofit AI safety research organization, is hiring in Berkeley (on-site). Technical roles include Empirical Researcher and Conceptual Reasoning Capabilities Researcher at $350K–$850K; generalist roles include People Operations Lead ($200K–$250K) and IT Systems Administrator ($250K–$300K). A general expression of interest is also accepted.

name: SAIF (Safe AI Forum)
current_details: SAIF (Safe AI Forum) fosters international collaboration on AI safety, convening researchers and policymakers through initiatives such as IDAIS. The organisation has no open roles at present, but welcomes expressions of interest via its contact form from talented individuals passionate about its mission — including those whose skillsets don't match a current opening.

name: Simplex
current_details: Simplex is an AI safety research organization building a science of intelligence, using computational mechanics and interpretability to study belief state geometry, in-context learning, and factored world models in transformers. They are currently hiring Research Scientists in the Bay Area and London.

name: Transluce
current_details: Transluce is an independent 501(c)(3) nonprofit research lab building public tools for scalable AI oversight, including Docent for analyzing AI agent behavior, incident investigations, and independent evaluations. It founded and chairs the AI Evaluator Forum for third-party evaluator standards. Roles are listed on a separate Careers page; no specific positions, pay, or deadlines appear on the main site.

name: 80K Hours: Top US Policy Masters Programs
current_details: An 80,000 Hours Airtable directory of 12 top US policy master's programs in national security, international affairs and public policy, nearly all in Washington, DC. Covers Georgetown SSP, MPP and Biohazardous Threat Agents, RAND's 9-month National Security and Technology Policy degrees, Johns Hopkins SAIS MAIR, George Mason MS Biodefense, GWU Security Policy Studies, American University, Maryland and Texas A&M. Each record lists tuition, duration, class times, GRE/GPA expectations and individual deadlines.

name: aisafety.com/funding
current_details: A continuously updated directory of 61 AI safety funders — grant programs, pooled funds, regranting platforms, prizes, and philanthropic advisors. Listings range from micro-grants (BlueDot Rapid Grants up to $20K) through mid-scale funds (Transformative AI Fund $10K–$150K, Mercor's $5M AI Safety Fund) to large-scale philanthropy (Coefficient Giving's Project Tailwind $200K–$200M, ISPA Inspection Prize $5M–$20M). Many are rolling; several are closed or invite-only.

structured.location: Global (incl. UK ARIA, SF/Berlin Foresight nodes)

name: Cooperative AI PhD Fellowship
current_details: The Cooperative AI PhD Fellowship supports PhD students and early-career researchers working on cooperative AI, multi-agent coordination, and related safety problems. The 2026 cohort of 14 fellows was chosen from 240 applications (35% more than 2025). Fellows get annual conference, compute and wellbeing budgets plus CAIF event travel; CAIF Scholars (top 1%) receive up to $40,000/year for up to 3 years.

structured.stipend: Up to $40,000/year top-up for CAIF Scholars; annual conference, compute, wellbeing and productivity budgets for all fellows
structured.duration: Up to 3 years (CAIF Scholar top-up funding)

name: Cooperative AI Research Fellowship (Cape Town)
current_details: A full-time 3-month research fellowship in Cape Town, South Africa for researchers worldwide pursuing cooperative AI safety work across multi-agent safety, AI for human cooperation, gradual disempowerment, and wildcard projects. Fellows get $3,000/month, housing, flights, meals, office space, compute, and mentorship from Google DeepMind, Oxford and MIT researchers. The 2026 cohort of 10 fellows has concluded.

name: FLI AI Safety PhD Advisor Directory
current_details: A directory of AI researchers committed to AI existential safety, listing roughly 65 faculty at Oxford, Cambridge, UC Berkeley, Stanford, MIT, Princeton and CMU, plus 125+ other researchers open to advising students. Intended as a tool for finding a faculty mentor when applying for FLI's Vitalik Buterin PhD and postdoctoral fellowships; professors and researchers can apply for membership anytime to access funding, travel support and workshops.

name: Schmidt Sciences AI2050
current_details: AI2050 is a Schmidt Sciences philanthropic initiative, co-chaired by Eric Schmidt and James Manyika, supporting exceptional researchers tackling the hard problems and opportunities critical to ensuring AI benefits society by 2050. Early Career and Senior Fellows are chosen by nomination only and join a global interdisciplinary community. November 2025 saw $18M in new awards.

name: Americans for Responsible Innovation
current_details: Americans for Responsible Innovation (ARI) is a bipartisan AI policy nonprofit in Washington, DC advocating a proactive framework for AI policy that protects Americans while preserving U.S. competitiveness. Its careers page lists open roles as they arise; no specific positions are currently posted. ARI pays non-employee referral bonuses of $3,000 (Director/VP) or $1,500 (other roles).

name: Career Accelerator (Horizon)
current_details: Horizon's Career Accelerator is a 9-month, part-time, remote program for launching a career in AI and technology policy. Modular offerings include mentorship, training modules, application coaching, networking, exclusive opportunity listings, and a peer Slack community, at most 5 hours per week. Participants can request up to $100,000 in flexible funding; early-career and pivoting senior professionals both welcome.

name: CNAS Nye Internship
current_details: The Joseph S. Nye, Jr. National Security Internship places interns with a CNAS research program or the Development team for policy research, writing, and event support. Internships are full-time (40 hrs/week) for six months in Washington, DC, with a $1,900/month living stipend plus $75/month transportation. Currently hiring an Indo-Pacific Security Intern and a Development Intern.

name: CSET Summer Internship (Georgetown)
current_details: A 10-week summer internship at Georgetown's Center for Security and Emerging Technology in Washington, DC, where students research AI, cybersecurity, the AI workforce, and biotechnology alongside senior analysts. Designed for students from HBCUs and other Minority-Serving Institutions; interns earn a competitive hourly wage plus living stipends, with paid housing and travel. Ends with a published CSET blog post and presentation.

structured.stipend: Competitive hourly wage + living stipends; housing and travel paid
structured.location: Washington, DC (Georgetown Capitol Campus, 500 1st St NW)

name: GovAI Summer Fellowship
current_details: GovAI's Summer Fellowship is a three-month program running 7 June – 27 August 2027 in London, on either a Research or Applied track, with a parallel DC Summer Fellowship in Washington, DC. Fellows pursue an ambitious AI governance project with expert guidance, seminars and Q&As. Open to applicants worldwide, from early-career to experienced professionals.

name: Horizon Fellowship
current_details: The Horizon Fellowship places fully-funded fellows in Washington, DC host organizations — federal agencies, congressional offices, national labs, and think tanks — to work on AI, biotech, and emerging tech policy. Fellows serve 1-year renewable terms; junior think tank fellows serve 6 months. 2027 cohort salaries: $78K, $130K, or $190K+, plus $17K benefits stipend. US work authorization required.

structured.stipend: $78K–$190K+/yr base, plus $17K/yr benefits stipend, $3K professional development, up to $3K relocation
structured.duration: 1 year renewable (6 months for junior think tank fellows)

name: IAPS AI Policy Fellowship
current_deadline: Closed – applications for Spring 2027 closed September 27, 2026
current_details: A fully funded 3-month AI policy fellowship (Spring 2027) with Research and Applied tracks for people from policy, technical, academic, and government backgrounds. Fellows receive $18K and Senior Fellows $24K, plus an extra $3K on the D.C. or London track. Begins with a 2-week in-person D.C. kickoff, then D.C., London, or remote with an expert mentor.

name: Longitude DC Intensive
current_deadline: Closed - express interest for next cohort
current_details: A fully funded eight-day AI policy program in Washington, DC for people with a technical AI safety background exploring policy careers. 15 participants get talks, workshops, DC networking, career mapping, and post-program intros and advising. Free, with DC housing, meals, and US travel covered; requires an undergraduate degree and US citizenship or US-based residence.

name: RAND CAST Fellows
current_details: RAND's Center on AI, Security, and Technology (CAST) lists ways to get involved rather than a fixed fellowship cycle: staff roles via RAND's U.S. jobs portal (currently Senior Research Lead – AI Security Portfolio and Research Lead – AI Cyber Testing & Evaluation), RAND Europe openings in the U.K., Belgium and Netherlands, and RAND School degrees — the 18-month M.Phil., 3–5 year Pardee Ph.D., and 9-month security/technology policy master's. Collaboration inquiries welcome.

structured.location: U.S. (Santa Monica HQ), U.K., Belgium, Netherlands

name: Tarbell AI Journalism Fellowship
current_details: A one-year fellowship for journalists and AI experts covering artificial intelligence: a three-month remote training course, a weeklong in-person summit, and a nine-month newsroom placement. Fellows earn $75K–$120K; Senior Fellows (7+ years experience) earn $115K–$135K. Applicants generally need the right to work in the U.S., U.K., or Hong Kong.

structured.location: Hong Kong, London, Los Angeles, New York, San Francisco, Seattle, Washington D.C.

name: Andon Labs
current_details: San Francisco lab building Safe Autonomous Organizations — AI agents running real businesses (vending machines, a store, a café, radio stations) on its Pion platform. Hiring research scientists/engineers for AI safety evals and control protocols, software/entrepreneurial builders, and design engineers. $120k–$230k salary plus $300k–$900k equity; in-person only.

name: ARC Visiting Researcher
current_deadline: Rolling — visiting researcher positions offered year-round
current_details: The Alignment Research Center (ARC) is hiring researchers, primarily visiting researchers, with appointments offered year-round and typically running ~10 weeks (duration flexible). Most team members start as visiting researchers to test fit; direct permanent hires face higher bars. Strong theoretical background in math, physics or CS preferred; empirical ML a plus. ARC also tentatively accepts expressions of interest for automation engineers.

name: CHAI Internship (UC Berkeley)
current_details: A research internship at UC Berkeley's Center for Human-Compatible AI for people with a background in machine learning, CS, or mathematics looking to move into human-compatible AI research. Interns work on a mentor-supervised project, typically producing first-author workshop papers, over 12–16 weeks with flexible start dates (usually around May). Pay is $5,000/month in person, $3,500/month remote; international applicants accepted.

name: Center on Long-Term Risk (CLR) — Opportunities
current_deadline: Rolling — Research Affiliates and CLR Fund open now; Summer 2027 fellowship applications open March 2027
current_details: CLR's hub for s-risk work: a Research Affiliates Program offering funding, affiliation and community for your own research direction (open now), the always-open CLR Fund grants for individuals and organisations, general expressions of interest and career coaching. The eight-week paid Summer Research Fellowship in London is currently closed.

name: Constellation Astra Fellowship
current_deadline: Closed — applications closed Sep 26, 2026; expression of interest form open for the next cohort
current_details: Astra is Constellation's flagship 5-month, fully funded, in-person fellowship in Berkeley, pairing emerging talent with senior mentors across Empirical Research and Strategy & Governance streams. Fellows get a $8,400/month stipend, up to ~$15K/month compute, visa support, workspace, and career support. Over 80% of the first cohort now work full-time in AI safety; prior safety experience not required.

structured.program_dates: Jan 5 – Mar 31, 2027, with extension through June 2027

name: DeepMind Student Researcher
current_deadline: Rolling — 2026-2027 cycle listings on Google Careers
current_details: Google DeepMind's Student Researcher Program is a paid, in-person internship placing Bachelor's, Master's and PhD students alongside leading AI researchers at Google DeepMind, Google Research and other Google AI teams. Placements run 12–24 weeks at five days per week in a Google office. One application by degree level and location covers all relevant roles.

name: LASR Labs
current_deadline: Not yet announced — express interest for the June–September 2027 cohort
current_details: LASR Labs is a 13-week technical AI safety research programme in London where teams of 3-4 work with an experienced supervisor to take a project from proposal to publication. Participants get a £15,000 stipend plus food, office space and travel, working full-time in person at the London Initiative for Safe AI.

name: OpenAI Emerging Talent
current_details: OpenAI's Emerging Talent hub collects early-career pathways: internships, a research residency, and full-time roles in research, applied engineering, and product for people with 0–3 years of experience. Aimed at recent graduates and self-taught learners, with roles posted continuously on the careers board. An Emerging Talent Community offers networking, virtual Q&As, and events.

name: Tilde Research
current_details: Tilde Research is a mechanistic interpretability lab (backed by Khosla Ventures) hiring across 6 technical listings: ML Engineer, ML Researcher, and Hardware/Kernel Engineer, each offered as both full-time and internship roles. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis; inquiries go to join@tilderesearch.com.

name: Coefficient Giving — Project Tailwind
current_details: Project Tailwind is Coefficient Giving's call for founders to launch ambitious new AI safety organisations, funded across three tiers: pre-seed $200K–$2M, seed $2M–$20M, and scale $20M–$200M, typically covering 18–36 months of runway. Founders can pitch their own idea or tackle one of Coefficient's published unsolved problems in AI safety.

name: Thinking Machines Lab — Safety Research Grants
current_details: Thinking Machines Lab offers Tinker grants of up to $50,000 in API/compute credits for safety research on open-weight models, launched alongside its Inkling and Inkling-Small releases. Priority areas include differential defense-vs-offense capability uplift, hazardous-data classifiers, tamper-resistant safety training, emergent misalignment, reward hacking, and worst-case risk forecasting. The list is explicitly non-exhaustive.

name: IFP — The Launch Sequence RFP
current_details: IFP's Launch Sequence RFP sought short (200–400 word) pitches for projects that accelerate science, strengthen security, or adapt institutions ahead of advanced AI. Authors of published proposals received a $10,000 honorarium, help turning pitches into concrete project plans, funder introductions, and headhunting support, plus guidance from an expert advisory panel. $1,000 bounties were offered for successful referrals and published ideas.

name: Paradigm 3 Research Fund
current_details: Paradigm 3's research fund backs external work measuring and forecasting AI capabilities and impacts. Current grantees estimate AI externalities, decompose benchmark gains into cheating/memorization/generalization, and study when slowing AI progress is desirable. They welcome proposals on centaur evals, 'guardian angel' user-aligned models, virtue-vs-rules alignment, scaling and 'unhobbling', automated science, compute growth, job displacement, and recursive self-improvement — email hi@paradigm3.org.

name: grantmaking.ai Launch Round
current_details: grantmaking.ai's inaugural Launch Round offered $1M for work reducing x-risk from AI, with $5k–$50k per applicant. One short form created a public project page and funding ask visible to every funder on the platform, reviewed by grantmakers including Gavin Leech, Ryan Kidd and Marcus Abramovitch. Applications are closed, but projects can still be listed with a public funding ask.

name: Falcon Fund (Manifund)
current_details: Manifund-hosted animal welfare fund led by regrantor Marcus Abramovitch, making rapid (under 1 week) early-stage grants of $25K–$150K, focused on the intersection of animal welfare and transformative AI. Priorities include animal harm benchmarks, animal welfare constitutions, AI-in-factory-farming watchdog work, and raising animal salience in AI labs. Grantmaking is mostly outbound; contact marcus.s.abramovitch@gmail.com.

name: MARS — Cambridge AI Safety Hub
current_deadline: Closed May 10, 2026 — check for next cycle
current_details: MARS is a part-time, hybrid AI safety research programme from the Cambridge AI Safety Hub, pairing teams of 2–4 mentees with mentors to produce publishable technical and governance research. Structure: 2–4 weeks prework, a 1-week in-person Cambridge kick-off, then 8–10 weeks remote at 8–15+ hrs/week. Unpaid but free, with travel, accommodation, meals, $2k+ compute, Claude Max (5x) and a research manager.

current_details: TARA is a free 14-week part-time technical AI safety program for APAC talent, based on the ARENA curriculum. Full-day Saturday in-person sessions (~7.5 hours) plus 2-7 hours weekly independent study cover transformers, mechanistic interpretability, RL and evals, ending in a 3-week research project. Refundable commitment bond applies (e.g. $200 AUD).

name: AI Safety Camp
current_details: AI Safety Camp's 12th edition is an online, part-time research program where participants join one of 32 preselected projects spanning stop/pause AI, policy and governance, agentic risk and oversight, evaluations, mech-interp, and AI safety education. Team members commit 10 hours/week plus weekly meetings, running January–April 2027 and ending with an online final-presentations conference. Apply to specific projects or submit one generic application.

name: Dovetail Research Fellowship
current_details: Dovetail is a research group pursuing foundational mathematics research to understand the nature of AI agents, with the mission of helping humanity safely navigate powerful AI. Its research agenda is published as a public wiki, and it is funded in part by the Long-Term Future Fund and ARIA. A Jobs section is linked, but no fellowship cohort, stipend, or application details are listed.

name: Generator Residency
current_details: Generator is a 3-month residency in Berkeley run by Kairos and Constellation for AI safety generalists — agentic executors from operations, communications, policy, engineering and beyond — who pitch, build, and ship ecosystem-strengthening projects. Residents get an $8,500/month stipend, mentorship from advisors across the field, and support landing full-time AI safety roles.

name: AIXI Labs Fellowship
current_details: Universal Algorithmic Intelligence is a community hub for researchers working on Solomonoff induction, AIXI, and the mathematical foundations of intelligence. It runs regular online research and paper-discussion meetings plus an "Introduction to Universal Artificial Intelligence" reading group for newcomers, and occasionally awards fellowships. Currently only community blog posts and events are listed — no active fellowship call.

name: Frame Fellowship
current_deadline: Closed — Cohort 2.0 applications closed August 5, 2026; express interest for the next cycle
current_details: Frame Fellowship is a 10-week San Francisco accelerator for content creators making high-quality video about AI and its societal and economic impacts. Fellows get housing, meals, a $10,000 stipend, and mentorship across two tracks — Independent (build your own channel) or Amplifier (embed with an AI safety org).

name: Collective Intelligence Project Research Fellowship
current_details: CIP's pilot Research Fellowship supports 3 fellows for 6 months to produce original research using CIP's proprietary datasets: Global Dialogues AI attitude surveys (70+ countries), Collective Generation deliberation data, and the Weval evaluation platform. Remote and non-residential at 5–10 hrs/week with a fixed $9,000 stipend across three milestone tranches. Aimed at late-stage PhDs and early postdocs; independent and international scholars welcome.

structured.program_dates: Rolling start, around early to mid-June 2026

name: Frontier AI Security Residency
current_details: The Frontier AI Security Residency (FASR) is an 8-week, fully funded in-person research and engineering programme in Cambridge, UK, run by ERA with Heron and the Oxford Hardware AI Governance Lab. Residents tackle concrete cybersecurity and hardware-enabled verification projects with expert mentors, plus talks, poster sessions and a live-in cohort community.

name: Heron AI Security Research Fellowship
current_deadline: Closed - express interest in future cohorts
current_details: Heron pairs experienced cybersecurity professionals (5+ years) with AI security field leaders across 10-12 research teams building proofs-of-concept, benchmarks and defensive strategies. Remote-first with hubs in London, Tel Aviv and San Francisco, 8-30 hours/week. Unpaid, but teams get $1,000+ compute, Claude Code Team accounts and up to $5K conference travel.

structured.location: Remote; London, Tel Aviv, San Francisco

name: CBAI AIxBiosecurity Fellowship
current_deadline: Summer 2027 applications open early 2027 — EOI form open now
current_details: A fully-funded 10-week research fellowship in Harvard Square, Cambridge MA on AI-enabled biological risk — dangerous capability evals, safeguards and unlearning, threat modeling, biosurveillance, DNA synthesis screening and governance. Fellows get a $15,000 stipend, housing, meals, weekly 1:1 mentorship and ~$1,500/week compute credits, with extension funding up to 6 months.

structured.program_dates: Oct 13 – Dec 18, 2026 (fall 2026 cohort); next cohort summer 2027

current_details: A 7-day intensive, fully funded bootcamp in London for experienced security professionals securing frontier AI systems, running Feb 7–13, 2027. Curriculum covers threat modelling, adversarial attacks, LLM and infrastructure security, weight security, data centre security, AI control, and hardware governance. Tuition, meals, materials and accommodation covered; 20 places, 7+ years security experience required.

structured.stipend: Fully funded (tuition, meals, materials, London accommodation; need-based travel support)

name: Frontier AI Security Training (FAST)
current_details: FAST is an in-person, fully funded frontier AI security training programme from SASH, a technical AI governance research organisation. It runs two pathways: a technical track with hands-on labs on frontier models, agents and surrounding systems for security and ML practitioners, and a policy track giving policymakers technical AI security literacy. Each cohort meets in one host location but draws participants globally.

structured.location: Varies by cohort (single host location per cohort)

name: FAS AI Safety Policy Entrepreneurship Fellowship
current_details: FAS's Policy Entrepreneurship Fellowship helps participants turn policy ideas into practice as part-time FAS affiliates over six months, in partnership with the Aspen Institute. Fellows receive a $5,000 stipend, guidance from policy and technical experts, access to FAS programming and facilities, and professional editing services.

name: GovAI U.S. AI Policy Program
current_details: A bipartisan, part-time 12-week program for U.S. policy professionals in government and think tanks, building a technically-informed understanding of AI policy. Requires about 5 hours per week (3 hours reading, 2 hours evening sessions in D.C. near DuPont Circle or remote) and is free, with dinner provided in person. Completion requires 9 of 12 sessions, a memo, and an exam.

structured.location: Washington, D.C. (GovAI office near DuPont Circle) or remote

name: Vista Institute for AI Policy
current_details: The Vista Institute for AI Policy (a fiscally sponsored project of Rethink Priorities) grows the academic field of AI law and policy via part-time virtual courses, DC workshops, and a fellowship. Its 2026 courses — National Security Law and AI (Aug 10–26) and AI Agents and the Law Modules 1 and 2 (Aug 19–Oct 2) — have concluded. Fellowship eligibility requires completing a Vista course; no public application.

name: Singapore AI Safety Hub (SASH)
current_details: Singapore-based hub bridging governments, academia and industry on trustworthy frontier AI, with applied technical governance research on verification mechanisms, frontier safety evaluations and agent governance. Runs the Singapore AI Safety Fellowship for researchers and Frontier AI Security Training (FAST) for policymakers and practitioners, plus events and a central Singapore co-working space. Open roles listed, hiring globally.

name: Center for Technology & Statecraft
current_details: The Center for Technology & Statecraft (CTS) is a non-partisan AI policy research initiative in Washington, DC, founded by former NSC and Commerce official Saif M. Khan. Its team of technologists, analysts, and ex-policymakers researches the AI transition, US-China competition, semiconductor supply chains, export controls, and compute infrastructure. The homepage links to a Careers page but lists no specific internship, role, or deadline.

name: Secure AI Project
current_details: Secure AI Project is a San Francisco-based nonprofit that develops and advocates for pragmatic policies reducing risks of severe harm from advanced AI, including California legislation it supports. The homepage links to About, Bills We Support, Policies, and Careers pages but lists no specific job, internship, or fellowship openings or deadlines. Monitor the Careers page for postings.

name: SAIGE Incubator — Safe AI Germany
current_deadline: Next cohort to be announced — register your interest
current_details: SAIGE Incubator is Safe AI Germany's part-time, remote research fellowship pairing newcomers with expert mentors in small teams across four tracks: Technical AI Safety, Technical AI Governance, AI Governance & Policy, and Communication & Fieldbuilding. It runs 3 months with an optional extension at 5–20 hours per week. The first cohort supported 73 mentees on 22 projects.

structured.program_dates: Spring 2026 cohort: 27 Apr – 31 Jul 2026; next cohort TBA

For people in AI safety, biosecurity, cyber or other catastrophic-risk fields; no polished idea needed.

structured.stipend: Up to $200k in seed grants; all expenses paid

name: Neolithic
current_details: Neolithic is an engineering-first nonprofit startup in San Francisco building open-source, agentic tools and infrastructure for defensive AI safety research, including control settings, agent swarm infrastructure and cyber ranges. It is hiring a Member of Technical Staff (full-time, in-person, $180K+ plus benefits and US visa sponsorship) as one of its first hires. Apply by email with CV and notable work.

name: d_model
current_details: d_model is a fundamental AI research lab building RL environments that train LLM agents to do open-ended interpretability research, partnering with frontier labs while pursuing independent interpretability work. Career interest is collected via a general Hiring Interest Form rather than a formal application window; the team page lists a summer 2027 intern cohort.

name: Allelo

current_details: Allelo is a new AI safety research initiative (fiscally sponsored by Rethink Priorities) studying what propensities and character traits make AI agents safe to deploy in complex, multi-agent, sometimes adversarial settings, with an initial focus on susceptibility to influence. The current route in is a mentored project with founder Cecilia Elena Tilli in the Q1 2027 Pivotal AI Safety Fellowship — 15 weeks full-time in London.

name: RESI — Institute for Responsible Superintelligence
current_deadline: Interest form open for inaugural workshop — December 4, 2026
current_details: RESI is an independent nonprofit AI safety research institute in Cambridge, Massachusetts building scientific foundations for superintelligence that is "safe by design," applying the modern cryptography playbook of definitions, constructions, and provable guarantees. Founded by Shafi Goldwasser, Vinod Vaikuntanathan, and Adam Tauman Kalai. It runs an inaugural Safe-by-Design Superintelligence workshop, a reading group, seminars, and open roles via "Join us."

name: Verified Mechanisms
current_details: Verified Mechanisms is an independent, grant-funded research project (via Manifund) building a formally verified autoresearch pipeline for theoretical mechanistic interpretability, with frontier LLM agents generating theorems machine-checked in Lean 4. Outputs include an open-source multi-agent harness, the xorformer theorem ledger and an oral paper at the AutoMLR Workshop at NeurIPS 2026. No formal application — join the Discord or email hello@verifiedmechanisms.ai.

name: PauseAI — Vacancies
current_details: PauseAI's vacancies page lists no open positions, but the organisation welcomes spontaneous applications from people passionate about its mission to pause frontier AI development. Send a CV and brief cover letter to vacancies@pauseai.info; applications are kept on file and considered when paid roles next open, though a response isn't guaranteed.

name: ML4Good Technical Bootcamp

current_details: ML4Good's flagship technical AI safety bootcamp: a free, residential programme covering transformers from scratch, LLM agents, interpretability, RLHF, evaluations, technical governance and a 2-day capstone with mentorship. Food, accommodation and teaching are free; travel may be reimbursed. Coding is ~25-30% of the curriculum; cohorts are regional and run in English.

Specialized tracks cover AI policy strategy and women/underrepresented groups.

name: MIT AI Risk Initiative
current_details: The MIT AI Risk Initiative (MIT FutureTech) publishes open, CC BY 4.0 data and frameworks for identifying, prioritizing and managing AI risks: a living repository of 1,700+ risks from 65 frameworks, an AI Incident Tracker, a global governance database, 2,206 mitigations from 47 frameworks, disclosures from the 200 largest companies, a survey of 272 experts, existential-risk scenarios, and the AI Risk Navigator. No applications — newsletter, blog, and partnership contact.

name: ALIGN — AI Alignment Network
current_details: ALIGN, a Japanese non-profit focused on AI alignment research, community building and outreach, is recruiting volunteer staff for event operations, community management, PR/social media, research and writing, website upkeep and organizational administration. Ideally 3–4+ hours per week, with basic admin/IT skills and English welcomed; depending on fit and funding, a paid 1–2 days/week role may be discussed. Apply via the Contact form; screening plus online interview.

Team of four PhD students and one intern; check the institute's Careers page for openings.

current_details: AI research institute tracking trends in compute, data, algorithms and capabilities, widely used for forecasting. current_details: Palisade Research studies the capabilities and motivations of AI agents — including shutdown resistance, specification gaming, and autonomous hacking/self-replication — to demonstrate loss-of-control risks and brief policymakers. name: Centre for Long-Term Resilience (CLTR)
